title: The Distortion Penalty answers a structural incentive flaw with discretion rather than a formula
content:
A.2.4.1.2.2.1.1.2.3.1 defines the Distortion Penalty as "a discretionary penalty designed to mitigate the potential misalignment caused by the asymmetric nature of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation." The Core Executor Agents, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, "may assess a penalty of up to 100% of Total Allocation System Profit... if it determines that a Prime's decisions were distorted by this incentive structure."

Two things are unusual. The trigger is a judgment about **motivation** — that decisions were distorted — rather than about any observable threshold being crossed. And the range runs all the way to complete confiscation of allocation profit, with no gradation specified.

The reasoning is defensible: the flaw being corrected is an incentive, and incentives are exploited in ways a formula cannot enumerate in advance. Any bright-line test would itself become the thing optimised against, reproducing the original problem one level up. Facing a discretionary penalty of unbounded size, a rational Prime must weigh how its choices will *look* to reviewers, which restores some of the caution the missing downside removed.

The cost is that a Prime cannot compute its expected return, since an unquantifiable haircut sits on top of it — and unpredictable enforcement discourages legitimate activity along with distorted activity. The Atlas accepts this as the price of shipping a simplified settlement early.

The contrast with its sibling is instructive: the Low Yield penalty in A.2.4.1.2.2.1.1.2.3.2 is explicitly "formulaic" for a behaviour that is measurable, while distortion — which is not — gets discretion. The Atlas matches instrument to observability rather than applying one style throughout.
description: Core Executor Agents with the Risk Advisor may take up to 100% of a Prime's Total Allocation System Profit if they judge its decisions were distorted by the asymmetric settlement structure.
